reason: The evidence the verifier offered was weak and partly self-defeating, but the line itself survives, because the Markmann text was found and read. WORDING, NOW FROM THE TRANSLATION: a scan of Black Skin, White Masks, Pluto Press, London, 1986, whose title page reads “Translated by Charles Lam Markmann” and whose copyright page reads “Translation Copyright 1967 Grove Press, Inc.”, was extracted in full. Its last two lines, after “At the conclusion of this study, I want the world to recognize, with me, the open door of every consciousness”, are “My final prayer:” and “O my body, make of me always a man who questions!” That is the shipped line word for word, including the exclamation mark, and it is the last thing in the book. The evidence’s admission that no page scan of the Grove text was seen is answered. THE ATTACK THAT LANDED, ON THE EVIDENCE RATHER THAN THE LINE: the verifier argued that the Philcox translation is separately attested with different wording, and cited thecharnelhouse.org for it. That page in fact prints the Markmann wording, “My final prayer: O my body, make of me always a man who questions”, against the page number 206, which is Philcox pagination. It conflates the two translations rather than telling them apart, so it cannot carry the argument it was asked to carry. The distinction is real all the same: Philcox, 2008, renders the French “fais de moi toujours un homme qui interroge” as “always make me a man who questions”, and that is the drift this line must not take. The shipped wording is Markmann’s and the source names Markmann, so the line is safe; the evidence field should say what was actually read. LOCATOR, A CORRECTION: Markmann does not head the final chapter “Conclusion”. It is chapter eight, “By Way of Conclusion”, rendering Fanon’s “En guise de conclusion”. The source should say so, which is the betterCitation. The claim that this is the final sentence is right. TYPOGRAPHY, A CAUTION NOT A REFUTATION: Markmann sets the two clauses as two short lines on the page. The passage is prose, not verse, so rule 7 is not engaged and running them as one sentence on the colon Fanon himself puts there is standard; an editor who wants to be exact could say “the closing lines”. ATTRIBUTION: Fanon, no trap on the misattribution list, and the line is his own, not a character’s and not one speaker reporting another. SCOPE: Peau noire, masques blancs, 1952, the translation 1967, philosophy, pre-1999, not scripture, film, lyric, proverb, business writing or oratory. PUBLISHABLE: the sentence needs no warning. TAG: Philosophy is defensible for the work, though Essay would also be honest. FORM: the source leads with the author’s name, carries no dash and no straight double quote, and runs 105 characters, 115 with the corrected chapter title, both inside the cap. SHIPPED.JS: not shipped, no near match, banned false, Fanon yearCount 0, atCap false. THEME, FOR THE EDITOR TO WEIGH: the fit with Justice and Service is real but indirect. It is a prayer to stay a questioner, in a book about what recognition is owed, rather than a sentence about what is owed; it reads well at six in the morning, and the month’s balance decides whether it earns a day.
